title: Neonatal age terminology used by the baby record (SMD_NEO)

age-ecrin.title: PedCRIN Tool: Neonatal trials and standard age groups: Points to consider, V 1.0 (Aurich B, Elie V, Mahmoudi N, Jacqz-Aigrain E), 22 March 2021
age-ecrin.publisher: ECRIN (European Clinical Research Infrastructure Network), PedCRIN project
age-ecrin.licence: Free access; no licence stated on the document (cites AAP Engle 2004 policy statement). Owner to confirm reuse.

rules.text: Gestational age is never rounded up.
rules.quote: Age is never rounded up in neonates (i.e. a neonate born at 24 weeks and 5 days gestation is a 24 week neonate).

rules.text: The neonatal period is below 28 days of life.
rules.quote: The neonatal period includes the first 27 days after birth (i.e. below 28 days of life)

rules.text: Postmenstrual age is gestational age plus chronological (postnatal) age.
rules.quote: PMA expresses age as a function of LMP, adding up GA and chronological (postnatal) age.

rules.text: Corrected age uses the expected date of delivery at 40 weeks; before it, corrected age equals GA plus postnatal age; after it, the weeks of prematurity are subtracted from postnatal age. Used under 3 years.
rules.quote: It is measured in weeks and months and takes the expected date of delivery (=40 weeks) into account

rules.text: Corrected age is used for premature babies under 3 years.
rules.quote: Corrected age is used for premature neonates under the age of 3 years.

examples.quote: For example a neonate born after 27 weeks and 3 days gestation and a chronological age of 12 weeks and 6 days has a postmenstrual age of 40 weeks and 2 days.
For example a neonate born after 31 weeks and 3 days gestation with a chronological age of 4 weeks and 6 days has a corrected age of 36 weeks and 2 days.
For example an infant with a chronological (postnatal) age of 50 weeks who was born at 25 weeks (40 - 25 weeks = 15 weeks premature) has a corrected age of 35 weeks (50 - 15 weeks).
